text: The scientific name of the domestic cat is Felis catus.
Domestic cats belong to the same mammal family, Felidae, as lions and tigers.
Cats are obligate carnivores: their biology is adapted to a diet based on animal tissue.
A cat can be social while still hunting alone.
Cats are often most active around dawn and dusk, a pattern called crepuscular activity.
The domestic cat is the only fully domesticated species in the cat family.
A group of cats may be called a clowder.
Carl Linnaeus introduced the scientific name Felis catus in 1758.
An adult cat normally has 30 permanent teeth.
Cats have 12 incisors and four canine teeth in their permanent dentition.
A cat’s carnassial teeth work together to slice food.
Kittens have 26 baby teeth before their adult teeth develop.
The tiny structures covering a cat’s tongue help it groom its fur.
Cats can aim their ears independently, listening without turning their bodies.
The small pouch along the outer edge of a cat’s ear is called Henry’s pocket.
Cats walk on their toes; this form of locomotion is called digitigrade walking.
A reflective layer behind a cat’s retina sends light back through the eye.
The reflective layer that improves feline low-light vision is called the tapetum lucidum.
Cats can hear frequencies much higher than humans can hear.
A cat’s ear flaps swivel to help locate the direction of a sound.
Cats have a third eyelid, called the nictitating membrane.
Cats have a scent-sensing vomeronasal organ in the roof of the mouth.
A cat’s whiskers are touch sensors, rather than a separate form of vision.
Cats have whisker-like sensory hairs above their eyes and near their front wrists.
A raised tail can signal that a cat feels friendly and comfortable.
A tail tucked low can signal fear or unease.
A fluffed-up tail helps a threatened cat look larger.
Slow blinking can be part of a cat’s friendly social communication.
A cat may flatten its ears when frightened or defensive.
Cats sometimes chatter while watching potential prey.
Cats rub their cheeks against objects to leave scent signals.
Feline behavior varies between individuals as well as between breeds.
Cats communicate using sound, body posture, touch, and scent.
Adult cats rarely use meowing to communicate with other adult cats.
Kittens use high-pitched mews to attract their mother’s attention.
A cat’s meow can be a greeting, a request, or a complaint.
A cat can open its mouth in a meow without producing an audible sound.
Cats can produce trills as well as the more familiar meows.
Purring may happen when a cat is anxious, not only when it is content.
Grooming another cat is one form of tactile communication.
The righting reflex lets a falling cat reorient its body toward a feet-first landing.
The righting reflex starts developing in kittens at roughly three to four weeks.
Tailless cats can still perform the righting reflex.
A cat’s flexible spine helps it twist during a fall.
A cat uses vision and its inner-ear balance system to identify which way is down.
Cats adjust their leg positions while rotating the front and back of the body.
Feline midair rotation obeys conservation of angular momentum.
The righting reflex does not make falls safe; cats can still be seriously injured.
A domestic cat can purr during both inhalation and exhalation.
The sound of a purr is accompanied by vibrations you can feel on the cat’s body.
Purring differs in loudness and tone between individual cats.
Cheetahs can purr too: the sound is not exclusive to house cats.
A purr’s rhythm changes with the animal’s breathing.
The mechanisms behind purring have inspired several competing scientific explanations.
Newborn kittens depend on their mothers for survival.
Kittens usually open their eyes around seven to ten days after birth.
A typical feline litter contains two to five kittens, though sizes vary.
Kittens practice stalking and hunting through play.
Young kittens learn from watching their mother and playing with littermates.
Kittens’ vision continues developing after their eyes first open.
The English word kitten came through Middle English from Old French.
Young large cats, such as lions, are usually called cubs.
A cat’s coat pattern does not by itself establish its breed.
Genes influence the color, pattern, length, and texture of feline fur.
The orange coat-color locus is located on the X chromosome.
Tortoiseshell coats combine orange and non-orange patches.
Male tortoiseshell cats exist, but they are uncommon.
The coat color breeders call blue is a diluted form of black.
Cream fur is a diluted form of red fur.
Mackerel tabbies have narrow stripes, while classic tabbies have broader swirling patterns.
Domestic cats trace their ancestry to African wildcats.
Rodents around early farming settlements helped draw wildcats toward people.
The domestication of cats was a gradual process rather than one single event.
Maritime trade helped cats spread beyond their early domestic range.
The Silk Road was one route along which domestic cats dispersed.
Domestic cats retain many behaviors found in their wild ancestors.
The genus Felis includes the domestic cat and several small wild cats.
The black-footed cat is one of the smallest members of the genus Felis.
The jungle cat is larger than the other living Felis species.
The name Felis comes from a Latin word for cat.
Felis species typically have pupils that narrow to vertical slits.
The Kellas cat of Scotland is a hybrid of domestic cat and European wildcat.
A member of the cat family is called a felid.
Living cats are divided into the subfamilies Pantherinae and Felinae.
Felids inhabit environments ranging from forests to deserts and mountains.
Cat-family tongues have firm papillae that help with grooming.
The cat family includes species active by day as well as by night.
The extinct saber-toothed cats belonged to a different felid subfamily from living cats.
Cats can learn new behaviors through trial and error.
Kittens acquire skills by observing their mothers.
Psychologist Edward Thorndike studied cats learning to escape puzzle boxes.
Cats have demonstrated object permanence: an object can still exist when hidden.
Play helps kittens develop skills they will use as adults.
Researchers study feline intelligence using memory and problem-solving tasks.
The Siamese breed developed from cats native to Thailand, formerly known as Siam.
Siamese cats’ pointed coloring involves a temperature-sensitive form of albinism.
The Siamese is known for blue eyes and a colorpoint coat.
The Balinese is a long-haired relative of the Siamese.
Crosses between Siamese and Persian cats helped produce the Himalayan.
Siamese-type cats appear in the Thai manuscripts known as the Cat-Book Poems.
The Maine Coon is the official state cat of Maine.
Maine Coons are known for their large size and dense, long coats.
The Maine Coon developed from a North American cat landrace.
Maine Coons appeared in American cat shows in the nineteenth century.
The Maine Coon is often nicknamed the gentle giant.
Stories about Maine Coons descending from raccoons are myths, not breed history.
The Bengal breed originated through crosses between domestic cats and Asian leopard cats.
Bengals can have spotted, rosetted, or marbled coat patterns.
The name Bengal comes from the Asian leopard cat’s scientific name.
Jean Mill played a major role in developing the modern Bengal breed.
The International Cat Association granted Bengals championship status in 1991.
Long-haired Bengals can occur when both parents carry the recessive long-hair trait.
Ann Baker developed the Ragdoll breed in California during the 1960s.
Ragdolls have blue eyes and a colorpoint coat.
The Ragdoll has a semi-long coat.
The name Ragdoll refers to the breed’s reputation for relaxing when picked up.
A cat named Josephine was central to the foundation of the Ragdoll breed.
Ragdoll breed development began in Riverside, California.
The Sphynx is also called the Canadian Sphynx.
The Sphynx breed was developed from naturally occurring hairlessness mutations.
Sphynx cats may have fine hairs rather than being entirely hairless.
Sphynx cats can have whiskers, broken whiskers, or no whiskers.
Patterns normally seen in fur can also appear on a Sphynx cat’s skin.
A hairless kitten named Prune was born in Toronto in 1966.
British Shorthairs are known for stocky bodies and broad faces.
The British Blue has a gray-blue coat and copper-colored eyes.
British Shorthairs also come in tabby and colorpoint patterns.
The British Shorthair breed was developed from British domestic cats.
British Shorthairs appeared at the Crystal Palace cat show in 1871.
The British Shorthair has a short but notably thick coat.
Abyssinians have ticked coats, with different color bands on individual hairs.
The Abyssinian is sometimes nicknamed the Aby.
The Abyssinian breed’s name refers to Abyssinia, now Ethiopia.
Abyssinians are often described as active, curious cats.
The Governing Council of the Cat Fancy recognized Abyssinians in 1929.
The modern Abyssinian breed was developed in the United Kingdom.
A cat’s purr can communicate more than contentment; context matters when interpreting it.
